question.problem: By the multiplicative property of congruences, $73\cdot 88≡$
question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}73 & ≡14\cdot 5+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡14\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 88 & ≡17\cdot 5+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡17\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}73\cdot 88 & ≡3\cdot 3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡9\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡5+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
73\cdot 88≡4\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$
